suggestions.title: Let the dev server take its port from the environment so the startup test never skips
suggestions.why: scripts/start.js hardcodes port 4178 (lines 3 and 9), and test/start.test.js therefore degrades to t.diagnostic("Port 4178 is already used; checking occupied-port failure only") when that port is busy, so its startup assertion (printed address plus a 200 from `/`) never runs. README.md line 36 tells users to keep `npm start` running in one terminal and the "Run the tests" section tells them to run `npm test` in another, so the documented workflow is exactly the case where the startup check silently disappears and a broken startup path can reach main.
suggestions.body:
## Request

Read the port from `process.env.PORT` in `scripts/start.js` (default 4178, still bound to 127.0.0.1) and have `test/start.test.js` start the server on a port it knows is free instead of hardcoded 4178.

## User outcome

`npm test` verifies that the demo server actually starts on every run, including while a developer keeps `npm start` running as the README instructs. `npm start` still serves http://127.0.0.1:4178/ unchanged.

## Acceptance

- `npm start` with no `PORT` prints and serves `http://127.0.0.1:4178/` exactly as today.
- With `PORT` set to a free port, the server binds that port and prints that URL.
- An unusable port (occupied, or not a valid number) prints one line to stderr, nothing to stdout, and exits with code 1, as the occupied-port case does today.
- `test/start.test.js` reserves a free port, passes it to the spawned process, asserts the printed address and a 200 from `/`, and keeps its occupied-port assertion on that same port.
- The test no longer emits the "Port 4178 is already used" diagnostic branch, and `npm test` passes with the demo server already running.
- The 95% branch-coverage gate in CI still passes.

## Evidence

- `scripts/start.js:3` and `scripts/start.js:9` hardcode the address and port.
- `test/start.test.js:21` skips the startup assertions when 4178 is in use.
- `README.md:36` asks the reader to keep `npm start` running; `README.md` "Run the tests" asks for `npm test`.

## Not included

No config file, no change to the 127.0.0.1 bind address, no auto-increment or fallback port, no HTTPS.

suggestions.title: Show an explanation instead of an empty checklist when the page script fails to load
suggestions.why: index.html ships an empty `<ul id="list">` (line 28) and a `#empty-list` paragraph that starts empty and `hidden` (line 29), so every list state comes from src/app.js. If that module fails to load or throws (blocked script, network error, older browser), a visitor of the live demo sees a checklist card with no items and no message; the only fallback is the `<noscript>` paragraph at index.html:37, which does not cover a module that fails after JavaScript is enabled.
suggestions.body:
## Request

Give the checklist area a static fallback that is shown when `src/app.js` never renders, and let `src/app.js` replace it on its first render.

## User outcome

Someone opening the demo when the page script fails sees a sentence telling them the checklist did not load and to refresh, instead of an empty box that looks like a broken sample.

## Acceptance

- With `src/app.js` blocked in the browser (or replaced by a module that throws), the checklist card shows readable text, for example "The checklist did not load. Refresh the page to try again."
- In a normal run that text is gone once the list renders; no per-filter empty-state behaviour in `src/app.js` changes.
- The existing `<noscript>` message and the per-filter empty states (`all`, `active`, `done`) are unchanged.
- `test/server.test.js` asserts that the served `index.html` contains the fallback text, so a later edit cannot drop it silently.
- `npm test` and the CI coverage gate pass.

## Evidence

- `index.html:28-29`: the list starts empty and the empty-state paragraph starts hidden and with no text.
- `index.html:37`: only the JavaScript-disabled case is covered today.
- `src/app.js` is the only writer of `#list` and `#empty-list`.

## Not included

No change to how tasks are stored or filtered, no loading spinner or animation, no new dependency.

suggestions.title: Expose the CI coverage gate as an npm script
suggestions.why: The 95% branch-coverage gate lives only inside .github/workflows/ci.yml as an inline command with three long flags, while package.json exposes only `start` and `test`. A contributor, or an agent delivering a change in a copy of this demo, has no local command that reproduces the gate the pull request must pass, so a coverage failure is only discovered after a CI round trip; the threshold and the measured files are invisible outside the workflow file.
suggestions.body:
## Request

Add a `coverage` script to `package.json` that runs the same command CI uses, and call it from the coverage step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` instead of repeating the flags.

## User outcome

`npm run coverage` fails locally for the same reason CI would, before a pull request exists.

## Acceptance

- `npm run coverage` runs `node --test` with `--experimental-test-coverage`, the same `--test-coverage-include` entries (`scripts/server.js`, `src/todo.js`), `--test-coverage-branches=95`, over `test/server.test.js` and `test/todo.test.js`.
- The Node 22 coverage step in CI runs `npm run coverage` and fails on the same threshold; the workflow no longer duplicates the flags.
- Lowering branch coverage in `src/todo.js` or `scripts/server.js` makes `npm run coverage` exit non-zero locally.
- The "Run the tests" section of README.md documents `npm run coverage` next to `npm test`.

## Evidence

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, step "Check server and list branch coverage", is the only place the threshold is written.
- `package.json` has no dependency on that gate, nothing for a contributor or agent to run.
- `README.md` "Run the tests" mentions only `npm test`.

## Not included

No change to the threshold, to the measured files, or to which test files run; `src/app.js` stays outside the coverage gate until it has tests.
